questions.q: What does STRING_AGG(Color, ', ') do when used with GROUP BY ProductSubcategoryID?
options: Concatenates every Color value within each subcategory group into one comma-separated string
Counts how many distinct colors exist per subcategory
Returns only the first Color value found in each group
Averages the lengths of the Color strings per group
questions.explain: STRING_AGG is an aggregate function that joins every value in a group into a single string using the given separator.

questions.q: What is guaranteed about row order WITHOUT a WITHIN GROUP clause on STRING_AGG?
options: Nothing — the concatenation order isn't guaranteed
Values are always concatenated in ascending order
Values are always concatenated in the order they were inserted
Values are always concatenated in reverse alphabetical order
questions.explain: Without WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...), SQL Server is free to process the group's rows in any order it finds convenient.

questions.q: What does STRING_AGG(Color, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Color ASC) guarantee?
options: The concatenated colors appear in a deterministic, alphabetically ascending order
Only the first color alphabetically is returned
Duplicate colors are automatically removed
The separator is ignored when ORDER BY is used
questions.explain: WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) makes STRING_AGG's concatenation order explicit and repeatable.

questions.q: How does STRING_AGG handle NULL values in the group by default?
options: It skips them automatically, without needing a WHERE ... IS NOT NULL filter
It raises an error if any value is NULL
It inserts an empty string with an extra separator for each NULL
It stops concatenating as soon as it hits a NULL
questions.explain: Like other aggregate functions, STRING_AGG simply excludes NULL values from the result rather than representing them specially.

questions.q: Which SELECT clause does STRING_AGG belong in, relative to GROUP BY?
options: The SELECT list, exactly like SUM or COUNT — it's an aggregate function
It can only be used in a WHERE clause
It must be used in a separate query joined back to the original
It replaces GROUP BY entirely
questions.explain: STRING_AGG is an aggregate function and is used in the SELECT list alongside GROUP BY, just like any other aggregate.
